surfaced-conflict.claim: The frozen Trial 5 capture cannot support total seal re-verification offline, so the strict certificate truthfully refuses the frozen replay even though the live path is sound.
evidence: The capture script itself asserted (= record decoded) and the capture text is reproduced byte-for-byte by decode->encode->pr-str (probe, 2026-10-22), so no data was lost under EDN equality.
objective-pin and evidence-pin DO recompute from the frozen capture (sp/objective-pin and evidence/evidence-pin match).

menu-pin and carrier-pin do NOT recompute (family-selection/sealed-menu-pin and sp/carrier-pin mismatch), and they still mismatch under recursive canonicalization: all-inner-sets sorted, all-inner-maps sorted by pr-str key, top-level array-map/sorted orders -- three variants tried, all fail.

Therefore the live pr-str input to the seal pins differed in serialization order from anything reproducible from the capture. The pins hash pr-str bytes, so any offline byte-verification of these two pins is impossible from this artifact.
Trial 5 itself passed verify in-process (activated-carrier was non-nil, :chosen present), so the LIVE path verifies fine; only frozen replay of the seal pins is blocked.
surfaced-conflict.consequence: The frozen positive cannot be preserved AND full semantic verification enforced -- the two requirements conflict on this capture. Per the workarounds-forbidden rule I did not weaken verify or pin checks. The frozen-replay test now asserts the truthful refusal with the exact defect (:carrier-defect :selected-policy-seal) plus everything the capture CAN evidence (content bindings, recorded pins).
